overview.title: 📖 Overview: Measuring the Edge of Shabbat
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 35a–35b
overview.hebrewSource: כּוֹכָב אֶחָד — יוֹם, שְׁנַיִם — בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת, שְׁלֹשָׁה — לַיְלָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The Gemara continues its precise search for the boundary between day and night. It first pins down the exact fraction of a mil that twilight lasts, then follows Abaye and Rava outside at sunset to work out which horizon the mishna's 'eastern face' actually means. Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Chiyya offer physical landmarks on Mount Carmel for measuring twilight and for finding Miriam's well. The Gemara then reconciles Rabbi Yehuda's and Rabbi Yosei's twilight for priestly immersion and teruma-eating, gives a starlight test for nightfall, and closes with the six shofar blasts that walked the town from the fields, to the shops, to the lit Shabbat lamp.

slides.title: 📏 Two Disputes That Run in Opposite Directions
slides.subtitle: Rabba and Rav Yosef disagree on twilight's length — and, oddly, on vessel size the other way

boxes.title: Twilight (mil)
items: Rav Yosef: two-thirds of a mil
Difference: half a danka (1/12 of a mil) — Rav Yosef's twilight is shorter

boxes.title: Wicker Vessel (kor)
items: Rabba: permitted to move up to 2 kor; 3 kor prohibited
Rav Yosef: permitted up to 3 kor; 4 kor prohibited
Here Rav Yosef's permitted size is larger

callout.label: Abaye's proof:
callout.text: Abaye asked Rabba this in practice, and even a 2-kor vessel was forbidden — matching the mishna that a vessel holding 40 se'a of liquid (= 2 kor dry) is beyond the size of a 'vessel' for impurity, and so beyond the size one may move on Shabbat. From this Abaye derived that dry goods exceed liquid capacity by one-third.

slides.title: 🧭 Which Way Is the 'Eastern Face' of the Sky?
slides.subtitle: Abaye catches Rava looking the wrong direction

lines.speaker: Abaye
lines.text: I saw Rava gazing westward at dusk. But the baraita defines twilight as lasting 'as long as the eastern face of the sky is reddened' — why look west?

lines.speaker: Rava
lines.text: Do you think it means the eastern face itself? No — it means the face of the sky that causes the east to redden, which is the west.

lines.speaker: Alt. version
lines.text: Some say it was the reverse: Rava saw Abaye looking east and asked him the same question.

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: Same resolution either way — and your mnemonic is a window: light from the west lands on the opposite wall, so that is what one actually watches.

callout.label: Point:
callout.text: 'Eastern face' in the baraita describes the effect (a red glow visible in the east), not the direction one must look.

slides.title: ⛰️ Landmarks and Signs on Mount Carmel — and in the Sky
slides.subtitle: Physical tests for twilight's length, Miriam's well, and starlight nightfall
rows: Leave the sun visible atop Mount Carmel, descend to the sea, immerse, and emerge — that span is his half-mil of twilight
Climb Carmel and look for a sieve-shaped rock in the sea; Rav adds that any portable spring counts as ritually pure, like this well
One star = still day; two stars = twilight; three stars = night — and per Rabbi Yosei, only medium-sized stars count, not ones visible by day or only very late at night

slides.title: 📯 The Six Shofar Blasts of Friday Afternoon
slides.subtitle: Each blast moves the town one step closer to Shabbat

steps.content: 1️⃣ First blast: field workers stop hoeing, plowing, and all field labor; nearer workers wait for the farther ones so all enter town together
2️⃣ Second blast: shop shutters come down and stores lock up; hot water and pots are still on the stove at this point
3️⃣ Third blast: pots are removed, hot water is insulated, and the lamp is lit — a pause follows, long enough to fry a small fish or stick bread to an oven wall
4️⃣ Tekia–terua–tekia sounds, and Shabbat is formally accepted

callout.label: Two views on the third blast:
callout.text: Rabbi Natan says it signals lighting the lamp; Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says it signals removing tefillin, since they are not worn on Shabbat.

slides.title: 🎺 May a Shofar or Trumpet Be Moved on Shabbat?
slides.subtitle: The sexton's synagogue shofar meets the laws of set-aside (muktze)

nodes.content: ❓ A baraita permits moving a shofar but forbids moving trumpets on Shabbat — why the difference?
💡 Rav Yosef: it depends on ownership — an individual's shofar has a Shabbat use (pouring water for a child through its bent mouth); a community's shofar does not
🤔 Abaye objects: couldn't a communal shofar also give water to a poor child? And another baraita permits moving trumpets too, just like a shofar!

✅ Resolution: three baraitot track three tannaim — Rabbi Yehuda (only useful items may be moved), Rabbi Shimon (no set-aside restriction applies at all), Rabbi Nechemya (an object's primary function still bars it, even for another use)

summary.principle: The Sages pin down the boundary of Shabbat with painstaking precision — the exact fraction of a mil that twilight lasts, which horizon actually signals it, and the six-blast sequence and starlight test that publicly mark its arrival — while also debating which objects may still be handled once it does.

flowSteps.content: 📏 Twilight's length disputed: 3/4 mil (Rabba) vs 2/3 mil (Rav Yosef)
🧭 'Eastern face' of the sky actually means the west, which causes the east to glow
⭐ Nightfall test: one star = day, two = twilight, three = night (medium-sized stars only)

columns.content: 📯 Six blasts walk the town from field, to shop, to lit lamp and accepted Shabbat
🎺 Shofar vs. trumpet on Shabbat splits along three tannaim's views of muktze

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda's (stricter) twilight for Shabbat, but Rabbi Yosei's (later) twilight for eating teruma

quiz.q: What is the practical difference between Rabba's and Rav Yosef's measures of twilight?
o: Half a danka, i.e. one-twelfth of a mil
Exactly one mil and a half
quiz.e: Rabba holds three-quarters of a mil, Rav Yosef two-thirds of a mil; the gap between them is half a danka, or one-twelfth of a mil.

quiz.q: When the baraita says twilight lasts 'as long as the eastern face of the sky is reddened,' which direction does Rava say one should actually watch?
o: West — the face of the sky that causes the east to redden
It does not matter; any direction works
quiz.e: Rava explains the phrase describes the cause (the western glow) of the effect (the eastern reddening), so one watches the west, like light through a window landing on the opposite wall.

quiz.q: According to Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel, what does seeing three (medium-sized) stars indicate?
quiz.e: One star means day, two stars mean twilight, and three medium-sized stars mean night has arrived.

quiz.q: In the sequence of six Friday shofar blasts, what happens after the third blast according to Rabbi Natan?
quiz.e: Rabbi Natan holds the third blast signals lighting the Shabbat lamp (Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi instead says it signals removing tefillin).

quiz.q: Why does Rav Yosef distinguish an individual's shofar (which may be moved on Shabbat) from a community's shofar (which may not)?
o: Individual shofarot are smaller and lighter
An individual's shofar has a permitted Shabbat use — giving water to a child through its bent mouth
Community property may never be touched on Shabbat
Only individuals are obligated to hear the shofar
quiz.e: Rav Yosef holds that because an individual's shofar can be used to pour water for a child, it is not muktze; a communal shofar lacks any such use, so it may not be moved.
